workload: Identical to m1-wrap.json and t25-renderer.json: 4K fixed colour buffer (3840x2160), 240x63 grid, EVERY cell rewritten every frame through Session::putChar, then split, shaped, atlased and rebuilt. Unchanged on purpose so the milestones compare directly.
how_to_run: cmake --preset release && cmake --build --preset release, then KRAIT_TERM_BENCH=<frames> KRAIT_BENCH_4K=1 KRAIT_BENCH_WARP=1 KRAIT_BENCH_OUT=<json> krait-app.exe
why: M2 added no renderer code, so this run is a REGRESSION check rather than a new number: the question is whether a milestone of backend, session and parser work slowed the hot path, and the answer is no.

comparison_to_m1.verdict: Within noise of m1-wrap.json (180.0 -> 177.6 fps, 5.555 -> 5.630 ms). Both are vsync-bound at the panel's 180 Hz, so the fps figure is a CEILING and the cpu_avg_ms number is the one that carries information. rules/render.md's budget is 60 fps; this is 3x it.

hardware_leg.detail: Same condition M1 recorded and for the same reason: this machine has no usable attached display, so a hardware D3D11 device initialises and then a present with nowhere to go fails. KRAIT_GPU=hardware exits non-zero with no frames. That is exactly the case T26's WARP fallback exists for, not a renderer regression — but it means the last real hardware number is still T25's 140.7 fps, now two milestones old.
hardware_leg.what_would_close_it: One run of the how_to_run line above with KRAIT_GPU=hardware on a machine with a monitor attached. It needs no code.
